hero-title.purpose: The public page's one headline — the payoff, not the app name.

screen-title.purpose: The name of the current screen, deliberately lighter than a bold heading.

section-title.purpose: One step down from screen title, for a section inside a screen.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked caption over a control cluster or field — the only uppercase text in the system.

chord.purpose: Smaller and lighter than the lyric beneath it, so it's read as a cue, not sung.

tab.purpose: Geist Mono, monospace alignment for ASCII tab blocks only.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Resting card in light mode; none in dark.

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: A card that leads somewhere, lifted further; none in dark.

shadows.name: shadow-float
shadows.purpose: The floating reading control bar; kept (darkened) in dark mode too.

shadows.name: shadow-panel
shadows.purpose: Any popover — menu, reading panel, chord shape; kept (darkened) in dark mode too.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.value: background-color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease
motion.purpose: Default state transition for buttons and interactive controls.

motion.name: counter-roll
motion.purpose: The hero counters' rolling digit; has a prefers-reduced-motion fallback that disables it.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one accent-filled pill action on a screen.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; min-height: 2.75rem; padding: 0.5rem 1.125rem; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary { border: none; background: #97490f; color: #fffaf4; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #86400d; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #97490f; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default pill button — white fill, hairline edge, resting shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { border: 1px solid transparent; background: #ffffff; color: #16181d; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(22 24 29 / 5%); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #edebe5; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The standard raised container — the first step off the warm page.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border-radius: 1.375rem; padding: 1.375rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(22 24 29 / 5%); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1.1875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #16181d; } .ds-card-body { margin-top: 0.5rem; color: #5c626c; font-size: 0.875rem; }

components.name: Form Field
components.description: Text input on the warm page — hairline edge, resting shadow, 16px to stop iOS zoom.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; margin-bottom: 0.4rem; color: #8d939c; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-field { display: block; width: 100%; padding: 0.875rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #dcdad4; border-radius: 1.125rem; background: #ffffff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(22 24 29 / 5%); color: #16181d; font-size: 1rem; transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-field:focus-visible { border-color: #97490f; outline: none; }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Accent-soft pill — a count or short label, never competing with the chord accent itself.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 2.375rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #f4e7d9; color: #97490f; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Reading Control Dock
components.description: The signature floating control bar — one pill-shaped dock holding play/speed, with a popover panel for key/notation/size behind one button.
components.html: 1.0x
components.css: .ds-dock { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.5rem; background: #ffffff; border-radius: 1.625rem; box-shadow: 0 8px 30px -8px rgb(22 24 29 / 25%); } .ds-dock-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 2.875rem; height: 2.875rem; border-radius: 1.125rem; border: none; color: #16181d; } .ds-dock-play { background: #97490f; color: #fffaf4; } .ds-dock-open { background: #f4e7d9; color: #97490f; } .ds-dock-speed { flex: 1; height: 2.875rem; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 1.125rem; background: #edebe5; color: #5c626c; font-size: 0.875rem; }

components.name: Sheet Chord
components.description: A chord marking above a lyric syllable — the one thing on the reading screen that must stay unmistakable from the lyric under it.
components.css: .ds-word { display: inline-block; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chord { display: block; background: none; border: none; padding: 0; padding-inline-end: 0.45em; color: #97490f; font-size: 0.7em; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.4; } .ds-lyric { display: block; white-space: pre; color: #16181d; }

narrative.overview: Songbook reads like a sheet of paper laid on top of an app: warm, matte, unhurried, inset from the edges of the screen so the song itself — not the chrome around it — is the thing the eye lands on. Nothing here is decorative by default; every token exists because a specific reading condition demanded it. Light and dark are each their own considered surface, hand-tuned rather than one inverted from the other, because a tablet propped on an amp in a dark room and the same tablet at a kitchen table in daylight are both real, both designed for on purpose. The one color that is allowed to be loud — the chord accent, terracotta in light and amber in dark — is loud for exactly one reason: it marks the thing a player's eye must never mistake for a lyric. Everything else that borrows it (a badge, an active control) stays visibly quieter than the chords themselves, on purpose. This system explicitly rejects the cluttered, ad-driven chord-site aesthetic (Ultimate Guitar and its kind) and the generic flat-dark developer-tool look — a single neon accent on near-black. Depth here comes from a warm neutral palette and a considered surface ladder, not from gradients, glow, or noise.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white paper in light, near-black (not pure black) in dark — never a cold or clinical neutral.
One accent color, reserved first for chords; everything else that uses it is deliberately quieter.
A corner-radius scale keyed to each shape's job, not its size — nested shapes are always rounder than their container.
Elevation is a shadow in light, a border in dark — the mechanism changes per theme, the meaning doesn't.
Pills are the one shape reserved for actions (buttons); nothing else in the app is pill-shaped.

rules.name: The Chord-First Rule
rules.body: The accent color's primary job is marking chords. Any other use of it must read as visibly quieter than a chord on the sheet.

rules.name: The Two Designed Themes Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is not light mode, inverted. Every color pair was chosen independently for its own theme.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: DM Sans, in weight 400 or 500, for everything except tablature. No second display font, no bold above 600 outside chord names.

rules.name: The Shadow-Or-Border Rule
rules.body: A surface is never given both a shadow and a visible border for depth. Light separates by shadow; dark separates by a hairline edge, except surfaces that genuinely float, which keep a shadow in both.

dos: Do reserve the accent (Chord Terracotta / Chord Amber) for chords first; anything else using it must read quieter than a chord on the sheet.
Do design light and dark as two independent, hand-tuned surfaces — never assume a dark value by formula from its light counterpart.
Do use a shadow for elevation in light and a border (--edge) in dark; never both on the same surface.
Do size every corner radius by the shape's job (how nested it is), not by the shape's absolute size.
Do keep the pill shape exclusive to actionable buttons — a card, a field, a badge, none of those are pills.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce alternative for every animation.
Do hit a 2.75rem (44px) minimum control size anywhere a control is tapped repeatedly mid-performance.
donts: Don't build anything resembling the ad-heavy, cluttered chord/tab site aesthetic (Ultimate Guitar and similar).
Don't default to a generic flat-dark developer-tool look (near-black surface, single neon accent).
Don't use a side-stripe (border-left/right > 1px) as a decorative colored accent outside the sheet's own chorus/bridge indent.
Don't give a disabled primary button a faded/opacity treatment — drop the fill to the flat disabled state instead.
Don't let a translucent or blurred surface sit over the song sheet.
Don't introduce a second display font or a bold weight above 600 outside chord names.
